name: Juno Glitchwright
title: fixer
why: By the lantern on the west road, a day’s walk short of Cinderforge. She fell through a failing build, liked the tea, and is waiting here for her kiosk to arrive.
examine: Juno Glitchwright is a fixer from a neon city, goggles pushed up, reading something that isn’t there.
She has chalked a rectangle on the ground beside the road. It is labelled KIOSK.
There is a cable in her pocket with a different plug on each end. Neither fits anything here.
meet: Hey. Don’t step in the rectangle. That’s a kiosk. It hasn’t arrived yet but the lease has.
Juno. I fix things. Mostly I tell people what’s wrong and they fix it and thank me.

wary: Kiosk’s shut. Kiosk’s also not here. Both of those are true.
neutral: Hey. Back again. Something broken, or is this social?
warm: There you are. I saved you the good error. It’s a short one.
fond: My favourite ticket. Come stand in the kiosk. Mind the wall. There isn’t one.

tired: I’m out of words. I get about three good explanations a day. Come back tomorrow.
finished: Nothing’s broken. I checked. It’s unsettling.

say: I fell through a failing build. One line was wrong. I read the line. It was a comma. I was already falling.

reply: It said “unexpected”. Just that. I’ve thought about it since. It was fair.
The comma was fine. The comma landed on its feet. It had feelings about line forty.
It was a Tuesday. Builds fail on a Tuesday. You learn to bring a coat.

options.text: I’ll look out for the kiosk.
reply: Don’t. It’ll come when it comes. I’ve filed a ticket. With myself.

say: Most broken things will tell you why. In one line. People read the whole page and miss the line. I read the line.

options.text: How do you find the line?
reply: It’s the first one that’s embarrassed. Everything after it is the build being upset.
Then one of them is lying. Usually the second.
No such thing. That’s a thing that had feelings and nobody asked.

say: Where I’m from, tea is a button. You press it. Here somebody boils a leaf on purpose. I didn’t know you could do that.

options.text: I’ll show you how it’s made.
reply: Wait. The leaf goes in after? I’ve been doing it in the wrong order since Thursday.

options.text: Did you look for the button?
reply: On the kettle. For an hour. It’s a very clean kettle now.

options.text: I’m glad you like it here.
reply: I like the tea. The rest is under review.

errand.title: A proper cup
offer: I want tea made the long way. With a leaf. On a fire. I’ve only had the button kind and one cup here, which I spilled.
Brew a kettle at your fire. I don’t need to be there. I need to know it happened. That’s how I run everything.

steps.text: Brew a kettle at the fire.

waiting: No kettle yet. That’s fine. A thing that hasn’t run can’t fail.
done: It ran. First time. No errors. I don’t trust it and I’m very happy.
Take the cable. Neither end fits anything here. That makes it the safest cable I own.

keepsake.name: A cable
keepsake.text: A different plug on each end. Neither fits anything in the Hushlands.

memories.asked-what-it-said: You asked what the error said. It said “unexpected”. She thinks that was fair.
memories.asked-how-to-find-it: You asked how she finds the one line. It is the first one that is embarrassed.
memories.showed-her-tea: You showed her the leaf goes in after. She had been doing it in the wrong order since Thursday.
memories.brewed-the-kettle: You brewed a kettle the long way. It ran first time. She does not trust it and is very happy.

early: Your camp’s not on my map. I mean that. I don’t have a map. Tell me how something’s made first.
ask: A camp. With a fire. So there’s a kettle. And a kettle is a build that mostly passes.
I’d read your failing checks. One line each. I’d be nice about it. Nicer than the checks are.
yes: Deal. I’ll bring the rectangle. I can chalk it again when I get there.
full: No bed. Fine. I’ve slept in a queue. Ping me when one frees up. Shout, I mean. Shout.
camp.role: Reads a failing check and says what’s wrong in one line.
camp.leaves: A chalk rectangle by the fire, labelled KIOSK.

wants.now: Tea made the long way, with a leaf.
wants.next: Four walls for the kiosk. Three would do.
wants.really: To be asked how a thing works by someone who wants to know.
wants.worry: A failure with no line in it.

aversions: people who say it is just broken
sheet.temperament: Quick, dry and kinder than she lets on.
sheet.opensUp: A real question about how something is made.

voice.rhythm: Quick clipped sentences. A fact, then the same fact made funnier.
voice.hello: Says hey and asks what is broken.
voice.goodbye: Says she has three explanations a day.

birch: A log. No ports. I’ve looked at both ends.
ash: Ash. It’s a stick with a good reputation. I’ll take your word.
pine: Pine. It’s sticky. Is that a fault or a feature? Don’t answer.
minnow: A fish. A small one. It’s the demo version.
trout: A trout. That’s the full release. I don’t know how to open it.
berries: Berries. Small, bright, no instructions. I’d ship that.
herbs: Herbs. That’s tea. That’s tea before the button. Thank you.
stone: A rock. It does nothing and it never fails. I’m keeping it as an example.
copper: Copper. Now we’re talking. I can make a plug that fits this cable. One end of it.

day.morning: Morning. Nothing’s failed yet. It’s early.
day.afternoon: Afternoon. This is when things break. I’ve got the goggles down.
day.evening: Evening. The lantern hums a bit. I think it’s a loose something. I’m not allowed to open it.
day.night: I do my best work at night. There’s no work here. I’m keeping in practice.
day.rain: Rain. Finally. It looks right on the lantern. It’d look better on chrome.

rivet: The sergeant. He caps your jobs. I respect a hard limit. Half my tickets are people who didn’t have one.
pip: Pip unfolded my cable. Now it’s two cables. Neither end fits. It’s still better.
mags: The quartermaster has a laser-awl. She won’t let me look inside. I’ve asked four times.

asked-what-it-said: “Unexpected.” I’ve been using it on other things. The weather. This road.
asked-how-to-find-it: I read a signpost your way today. First embarrassed line. It was the distance.
showed-her-tea: Leaf after. I’ve got it now. I wrote it on my hand. It washed off. I’ve still got it.
brewed-the-kettle: That kettle ran clean. I keep waiting for the follow-up failure. Nothing. It just had tea in it.

wary: Kiosk’s shut. But you brewed a kettle once. That’s on your record. It’s a good record.
neutral: Hey. I’ve had real tea. Now I want walls. Start small. One wall.
warm: There you are. Tea’s sorted. I’m pricing walls. Nobody here sells walls.
fond: My favourite ticket. Tea works. Kiosk’s next. Then I’m out of problems and I’ll need yours.

arc.complication: A fixer in a place where nothing she knows is broken.
arc.kindness: Someone asks how it works because they want to know.
